solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Punitive damages constraining religious work

indicators.note: the first two words hold the answer locked inside them, straddling the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of Punitive joined to the start of damages

explanation.surface: A court orders punitive damages that hold up the publication of some sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the oldest scriptures of Hinduism, so one of them is a sacred text.

clue.text: Quality of life in London possibly under examination

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under means placed below, so the second part follows the first

blocks.note: a viva is an oral exam
London is one example of a city

explanation.surface: Studies are looking into standards of living in London.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' puts CITY below VIVA. A viva is the spoken defence of a thesis at British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is liveliness, the trait of being full of energy and spirit.

clue.text: Money given by party and country

blocks.note: a do is a party
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A political party and the state hand over funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, typically cash handed to a charity or cause.

clue.text: Author will go with millions for reading, perhaps to enlighten

indicators.note: one thing put in place of another: millions stands where reading stood

blocks.note: the setter, as author, says I'll
go is a polite euphemism for passing water
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
reading is one of the three Rs, so it stands for R, the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A writer reads aloud to a big audience hoping to enlighten them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author will go' is I'LL URINATE; swap its R for M and you get ILLUMINATE. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To illuminate a subject is to shed light on it, making it clear and so informing people.

clue.text: Minimum rent charged by original letters

indicators.note: charged here means loaded or filled, so the rent is filled up by the letters

blocks.note: a let is a rental
AS is the abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon, the original English

explanation.surface: Landlords of old set a minimum rent.
explanation.walkthrough: LET holds AS: LE(AS)T. 'Letters' looks like landlords, people who let property.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest possible amount, so it is a minimum.

clue.text: Less transparent individual authorising peacekeeping force?

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeepers
one who clears something gives approval

explanation.surface: An official who signs off on sending peacekeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a UN clearer; split, it is the comparative of unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is murky or opaque, so being more so is the comparative of it.

clue.text: Risible rites surprisingly hard to ignore

indicators.note: something surprising comes out in an unexpected form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Ridiculous ceremonies turn out to be strangely compelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irresistible is too strong or tempting to resist, so it demands attention.

clue.text: Dormant reptile taking shelter

indicators.note: the reptile takes something in, holding it inside

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: A snake lies inactive while hiding under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: ASP holds LEE: AS(LEE)P.
explanation.definitionFit: Asleep means not awake, inactive, which is what dormant describes.

clue.text: Looking back, you head off person

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end to its start
with its head off, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: ye is an old word for you
a being is a person

explanation.surface: Glancing over your shoulder, you cut someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking back' reads as one phrase but splits: Looking is the definition, back reverses YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing is watching someone or something closely, so it means looking at them.

clue.text: Give voice to battle-hardened soldier getting back from Afghanistan

indicators.note: the soldier receives something, which is taken inside him
the back of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of Afghanistan is used

blocks.note: a vet is a veteran, a seasoned soldier
the last letter of Afghanistan

explanation.surface: A veteran home from Afghanistan finally speaks out about the war.
explanation.walkthrough: VET holds N: VE(N)T.
explanation.definitionFit: To vent feelings is to express them openly, often anger or frustration.

clue.text: Left half-cut after pub sing song

indicators.note: cutting the word in half keeps only its first two letters

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
to carol is to sing joyfully
the first half of Left

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles out of the pub half-cut, that is, tipsy, and has a sing-song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the pub; 'sing song' looks like one phrase but splits into the verb and the definition. 'After' puts BAR before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is a Venetian gondolier's song or a piece composed in that rocking style.

clue.text: Extended time in prison revealed embarrassing things about guards

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: to out someone is to expose their secrets
a stretch is a prison sentence

explanation.surface: An exposé of a long jail term lays bare shameful secrets about prison officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like prison staff but is the containment signal; a stretch is British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Outstretched means reached out to full length, so a limb so held is extended.

clue.text: One-piece uniform involved in care for pet

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

blocks.note: to cat-sit is to look after someone's cat
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A uniform is needed by someone looking after a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-piece' is the definition, used as a noun, as with a swimsuit called a one-piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A catsuit is a close-fitting garment covering the body and legs in a single piece.

clue.text: Orient Express to start backwards, according to crew

indicators.note: only the start of the word is wanted, its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Express
sailors say astern for backwards

explanation.surface: The Orient Express pulls out of the station in reverse, the train crew say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient Express' reads as the famous train; split it, and Orient is the definition, Express the source of E.
explanation.definitionFit: Orient is a poetic adjective meaning of the east, as in the orient pearl.

clue.text: Crowd backs appropriate mechanism to decrease strides?

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it in support, so this part comes second

blocks.note: to trouser money is to pocket it, often dishonestly
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A crowd supports a suitable way to slow people's walking pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Strides is British slang for trousers, and de-crease means take out creases, though the surface reads it as lessen. To trouser money is to pocket it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouser press flattens trousers overnight, removing wrinkles and creases from the legs.

clue.text: Vile leaders of political union stopping in power

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters
to stop a gap is to plug it, so the letters sit inside the other word

blocks.note: regnant means reigning
first letters of political and union

explanation.surface: Nasty union bosses block the ruling party.
explanation.walkthrough: PU goes into REGNANT: RE(PU)GNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means repulsive, causing disgust, a close synonym for vile.

clue.text: I crew ship

blocks.note: India is the code word for I in the phonetic alphabet
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Someone states that they work aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: I, sounding like a pronoun, is only the letter spelt out as INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant vessel trading with India, especially for the East India Company.

clue.text: What’s played wearing red skirts?

indicators.note: a skirt goes round the body, so this word goes round the other

blocks.note: claret is red wine, and also a deep red colour
to be in a garment is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A riddle about some game played by someone dressed in red skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning goes round; claret is a red Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, a thing that musicians play.

clue.text: Relative in favour of internet gateway keeping one connected

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the gateway holds the other letters

blocks.note: pro means for
a portal is a website giving access to others
Roman numeral one
a device that is connected is on

explanation.surface: A family member backs an online service that keeps someone linked up.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO, then PORTAL holding I and ON: PRO + PORT(I ON)AL. 'Relative' looks like a family member but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proportional is in proportion, measured against something else rather than absolute, which is relative.

clue.text: Anxious about content of financial records

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside its outer edges

blocks.note: on means about, concerning
a ledger is an accounts book; its inside letters

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about what the company accounts contain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LEDGER and drop its outer L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means nervous and tense, unable to relax, which is anxious.

clue.text: Run through what dim author might write

blocks.note: the author, faint and wan

explanation.surface: Someone skims over what a dull writer might produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' suggests stupid but means pale, faint; the writer refers to themself as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a sharp point, as a sword would go through someone.

clue.text: Signal to handle Spooner’s domesticated horse

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

blocks.note: a nag is a horse, tame means domesticated; swap the initial sounds

explanation.surface: A rider signals how to handle a horse that has been broken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' means a name here, as in a nickname; the surface makes it a verb about controlling a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tag is a label worn to display a person's name, so it advertises what people call them.

clue.text: Best friend possibly right employee of mine

blocks.note: a dog is man's best friend, and a collie is one example
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Your closest pal might just be the right person to hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of mine' looks like a possessive, my employee, but mine is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a worker employed underground at a pit.

clue.text: Large plant company taking on a bean-counter

indicators.note: to take on is to take in, so the company holds the rest

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
a bean-counter is an accountant; CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A big factory firm hires an accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: CO holds A and CA: C(A CA)O. 'Plant' looks like a factory but is a tree; the cacao tree gives cocoa beans, a nice nod to the bean-counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacao is a tropical tree, a sizeable plant whose seeds make cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Wake guard behind curtains

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the guard follows the other part

blocks.note: it's curtains means it's the end, death
a watch is a guard on duty

explanation.surface: A sentry, roused from sleep, stands hidden behind the drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's curtains' is an idiom for the end; the surface makes them window drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake is a vigil held over a dead body, and a deathwatch is a vigil kept beside the dying or dead.

clue.text: Apparently, hen party’s make-up is sign of things to come

blocks.note: a hen party is made up of women
the guests seemingly lack a wife, abbreviated W, since the bride is not yet married; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: The look of a bride's party crowd tells you what the wedding will be like.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British pre-wedding night out for the bride and her female friends. Take W, for wife, out of WOMEN; the bride is not yet a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, an event taken as a warning or promise of the future.

clue.text: Engineer mentioned a way to improve faulty lines

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct it, so these letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An engineer has suggested a fix for broken power or phone lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' sounds like cables for the engineer, but means lines of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendation is a correction made to a text, improving a passage that contains errors.

clue.text: One teacher originally applied to higher education institution

indicators.note: originally points at the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: uni is short for university
the first letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A single teacher applies for a job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applied to' puts T against UNI.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing regarded as complete in itself, the number one.
